author: scoobydoo
text:
Astro, as much as I've tried to move from scalping to Set and Forget
trading, I've never manage to get it to work nearly as well either. It
sounds ideal, just set these trades..go away and do something more
useful with your time but in real life I find setting limits very
frustrating (when you are constantly watching the charts you can
sometimes make a decision to enter or exit a trade near a level when it
looks like it won't quite make it).

Anyway, my point is this .... look at your equity curve. Nice and smooth
 apart from that hiccup in the middle when you were trying to will
yourself towards Set and Forgets. Look at the difference in profit.
Scalping may seem stressful, but when u have a nice smooth upward slope
with very little drawdown..really..is it THAT stressful? Yes, it takes
up A LOT of your time. I may be wrong but we are all different and from
what I've seen you may be better suited to scalping. I myself just can't
 hold trades to faraway targets enduring huge retraces along the way.

Your results are great. I doubt anyone here will be able to beat those
returns by setting trade limit orders at the beginning of a day and
seeing how it's played out by market end. I would say to you there is NO
 NEED to change what you are doing. You have found WHAT WORKS FOR YOU
and that is the most important thing. If it's a question of stress due
to the amount of time in front of the PC I have a few suggestions...

1) At your current rate of account growth I think it is feasible you
could take more time off. Maybe a monday or friday to extend the
weekend...or a wednesday to break in into 2 days at a time. This is much
 easier to do as an intraday scalper as you can be completely flat with
no trades to even think about on your days off.

2) You could set a target for the week and if you reach it by wednesday then that's fine..rest of week off.

3) You can just trade the most volatile times around data releases.and
if that includes indices then DAX open, DOW open, DAX close, DOW close.
 maybe doing a few hours every day and taking the rest of the day off.

4) If you feel entirely comfortable in your scalping ability then what's
 to stop you doubling the risk on every trade? As long as you have good
control of your drawdown (which you definitely appeared to have before
the Set and Forget hiccup) then it really shouldn't be a problem and you
 could be on the path to making the same percentage growth with far less
 trades.

I'm, sure you are already well aware of the above points, but I just
wanted to encourage you to keep going with the scalping.....If it ain't
broke, don't fix it

author: Astrokillah
text:
Haanz, I trade via MT4. It let me set unlimited number of alerts, I
have it on my cellphone too so I set a alert on MT4 deskstop and when it
 is triggered it gets sent to MT4 android.

MT4 allows fast mouse clicking which is essential for scalp execution.
The only disadvantage of MT4 is I haven't been able to use anything
lower than 1min timeframe.

If you are practicing scalping on 1min there is no need to use
forextester. I have Forextester3 unlimited data version and I hardly use
 it to practice my scalping. An MT4 demo account is good enough for
practice.

My 2 cents :)

I scalped from FL to FL on 1-min chart. I don't count RR. I count $$. I
 trade NY session only. As far as number of trades per day, I just had a
 look at my statement, I had 22 trades on March-8, and 46 trades on
March-7.

It is impossible to learn how to scalp by reading people's journals, you
 just have to open a demo account and practice it on 1-min. No body
taught me how to scalp, but RTM taught me that price moves from FL to
FL, so that's the fundamental principle I followed.
